items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy Power Grid, NTPC, Info Edge among 26 stocks for dividend rewards
items.description: Under Sebi’s T+1 settlement cycle, investors need to purchase a company’s shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by the record date (November 6), making them eligible for the dividend.

items.title: Stock split alert! Last day to buy this Ashish Kacholia-backed multibagger smallcap stock ahead of record date for 1:5 split
items.description: After the stock split takes effect, her 10 shares will be split into 500 shares worth Rs 20 each, keeping the total value of her stock holding the same at Rs 1,000.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty200 pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 4, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Fee defaults push Sebi to pull the plug on 8 investment advisers
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has canceled the registrations of eight investment advisers for failing to pay fees. The affected firms include Karvy Investment Advisory Services, IDFC Alternatives, and six others. Non-payment of renewal fees dates back to December 2018 for certain firms and continues for others. Registered investment advisers are required to pay renewal fees every five years to maintain validity.

items.title: M K Sons Fine Jewels lists at 5.5% premium to offer price
items.description: Shares of M K Sons Fine Jewels were listed at ₹171 on the NSE on Wednesday. Shares were listed at a premium of 5.56% over the issue price of ₹162 per share. The stock closed at ₹162.20 per shares on Wednesday. The market capitalisation of the company stood at ₹913 crore.

items.title: RBI forms technical committee to deal with financial markets’ issues
items.description: RBI has created a technical consultative committee for financial markets to involve market participants in discussions. This committee will be chaired by the deputy governor responsible for financial markets regulation and will meet quarterly. It will focus on money, government securities, foreign exchange markets, and related derivatives. The terms of reference include market liquidity, trading systems, resilience, and emerging risks.

items.title: D-Street poised for a gap-up start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced gains as they extended their winning streak to five consecutive sessions. The Nifty 50 increased by 150 points while the BSE Sensex advanced by 383 points. Easing crude oil prices and optimism over US-Iran negotiations led to a broad-based buying in domestic equities. Additionally, foreign portfolio investors were net buyers, contributing to positive market sentiment.

items.title: Stocks in news: BSE, Lenskart, Nykaa, Bharti Airtel, LIC, Aurobindo Pharma and Nalco
items.description: Indian equity markets have enjoyed a remarkable stretch, registering gains for five consecutive sessions. The Nifty 50 index showed impressive growth, sparking optimism for a breakout beyond 24,000. Companies like Lenskart, Aurobindo Pharma, and BSE are in the spotlight as they report positive earnings. Experts advise keeping an eye on the support levels as the bullish trend persists.

items.title: 15 stocks to bet on as Indian markets look to rebound in Samvat 2083
items.description: Investors are entering the new Hindu calendar year with renewed optimism for Indian equities. Easing valuations, steady earnings growth, and improving foreign inflows are contributing to this positive outlook. The Nifty and Sensex have declined by about 8% in the previous year. Brokerages have compiled 15 stock ideas expected to outperform in the upcoming Samvat 2083. This presents potential opportunities for investors looking to regain momentum.

items.title: Foreign buying, softer crude lift Dalal Street; Sensex closes above 77,300
items.description: Following the US midterm elections, Indian investors are buoyed by hopes of decreased global trade tensions. The Sensex surged by 383.55 points, closing at 77,301.40, while the Nifty increased by 149.75 points to end at 23,960.60, highlighting a significant rebound for the indices. Analysts believe reduced geopolitical risks could enhance India's economic prospects, despite a mixed performance in Asian markets regarding US investments in AI.

items.title: Stock Radar: Down over 18% from highs! BSE stock breaks out from inverted head & shoulder pattern; time to buy?
items.description: BSE Ltd has shown signs of recovery after correcting over 20% from recent highs and finding support. The stock has broken above key resistance levels, suggesting potential bullish momentum in the coming weeks. Analysts recommend buying the stock with a target of Rs 3,850 and a stop loss below Rs 3,600. Recent market data indicates strong derivatives activity, supporting this positive outlook.

items.title: Sebi eases KYC norms for NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals, allows digital onboarding from overseas
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has relaxed Know Your Client requirements for overseas investors. This change enables non-resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and foreign nationals to onboard digitally. Individuals from FATF-compliant countries can now submit KYC details remotely without being in India. Intermediaries are allowed to rely on existing KYC records and conduct video verifications when necessary.

items.title: US midterm election impact: What it means for investors in equities, bonds and gold
items.description: The US midterm election outcome could influence equities, bonds, gold and emerging market flows, but its direct market impact may remain limited. A weaker dollar and lower Treasury yields could support emerging markets and gold, while Federal Reserve policy, crude oil prices and AI spending remain key drivers for investors.

items.title: Uday Kotak says $700 bn outstanding FII payments will boost market, sees AI worries driving flows to India
items.description: Veteran banker Uday Kotak expects India to benefit from a potential reversal in global investment flows as concerns over excessive AI spending weigh on US markets. He highlighted $700 billion in outstanding foreign portfolio investments, flagged the possibility of further RBI rate hikes and advised investors to focus on quality stocks and medium-term strategies.

items.title: Bharat Electronics among 5 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On November 4, five Nifty 50 stocks that gained over 3% appeared on StockEdge's White Marubozu bullish scanner, according to its technical scan data.A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis in which the opening price is the lowest and the closing price is the highest for a given period. It is represented by a long white or green candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow.The pattern reflects strong upward price movement during the session, indicating that buyers remained in control from the opening bell to the close. Traders commonly study it as a signal of bullish momentum.

items.title: Prime Focus shares drop 7% as Ramayana Part 1 makes debut across 5,510 shows today
items.description: Prime Focus shares fell as much as 7% as Ramayana made its theatrical debut. Despite high expectations and a reported Rs 4,000-crore budget, early box-office collections came in below trade projections, putting the spotlight on the film's opening performance.

items.title: Rs 40,000 crore in 13 days! Is the great FII reversal finally here to save Nifty bulls?
items.description: Foreign institutional investors have pumped nearly Rs 40,000 crore into Indian equities in 13 trading sessions, raising hopes of a sustained reversal after months of heavy selling. Falling crude oil prices, improving corporate earnings, attractive valuations, a weaker dollar and expectations of an LTCG tax cut are driving the renewed optimism.

items.title: Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland shares rocket up to 12%. Here are 2 reasons fuelling the sharp surge
items.description: Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors shares rallied, tracking a sharp fall in crude oil prices and a broader market recovery amid hopes of a negotiated settlement to the Iran conflict. Brent crude plunged nearly 9% in the previous session and extended losses on Thursday, easing fuel cost concerns for fleet operators.

items.description: Muhurat Trading 2026 date & time: BSE, NSE and MCX will conduct the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session on November 8 to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083. Here are the complete timings for equity, commodity, IPO and newly listed stocks, along with details on settlement and delivery.

items.title: Pills are paying off! Pharma stocks lead 2026 rally with up to 112% return
items.description: In 2026, India's pharmaceutical stocks are making headlines with impressive year-to-date gains. This surge is driven by strong domestic demand alongside enhanced profitability from new product launches. Notable players like Laurus Labs and Gland Pharma have recorded remarkable returns, topping 100%. Amid challenges faced by other sectors, the pharmaceutical field demonstrates resilience. Analysts are optimistic but advise exercising caution regarding potential market volatility and the durability of this sector's performance.

items.title: Trump’s pain makes D-Street bulls gain! IndiGo, Asian Paints, other crude-sensitive stocks rally up to 8% as oil drops below $95
items.description: Paint makers, airlines, tyre companies and OMCs rallied as crude oil prices plunged nearly 10%, falling below $95 a barrel. Lower oil prices raised hopes of easing input and fuel costs, while Trump's midterm setback added to the positive market sentiment.

items.title: These mid-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and upside potential of up to 28%, according to analysts
items.description: Global markets on Wednesday celebrated the outcome of the US mid-term election as well as a sharp drop in oil prices. Oil prices, which at the end of last week were at about $118 to the barrel, are now under $95. The hope clearly is that Democrat control of both chambers of the US Congress will pressure the Trump administration to pursue a diplomatic end to the conflict with Iran in the Gulf.

items.title: Cummins India shares crash 15% after Q2 net profit falls 19% YoY, margins take 680 bps hit
items.description: Cummins India shares plunged after the company reported a 19% year-on-year decline in Q2FY27 net profit, while EBITDA margin contracted sharply. Higher commodity and freight costs, along with an unfavourable product mix, weighed on profitability despite growth in domestic sales and exports.

items.title: Ather Energy shares fall 4%, snap 5-day gaining streak. What’s triggering the sharp fall?
items.description: Ather Energy shares ended a five-session winning streak as the shareholder lock-in period expired, making 21% of its outstanding equity eligible for trading. The development comes after the EV maker reported its first quarterly profit, while Nomura retained its Buy rating.

items.title: Pricol shares jump 8% after Q2 results; net profit rises 33% YoY to Rs 85 crore
items.description: Pricol shares rallied after the company reported strong Q2FY27 results, with consolidated net profit rising 33% and revenue increasing 35% year-on-year. The company also highlighted business recognitions, operational priorities and a positive trend across key moving averages.

items.title: Explained: 5 reasons why Trump’s midterm election setback matters for Indian markets and economy
items.description: Donald Trump’s midterm election setback has triggered a global market rally, with Indian equities gaining sharply. Lower crude oil prices, a weaker dollar, potential FII inflows, reduced tariff risks and changing US interest rate expectations could reshape India's economic outlook. Here are five key ways the political shift could impact markets.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
items.description: Indian markets staged a powerful rally, with Sensex jumping 2,009 points and Nifty gaining 576 points. Improved global sentiment, easing crude prices, US midterm election results, foreign investor buying and strong Q2 earnings lifted market capitalisation above Rs 500 lakh crore.

items.title: Marico among 10 stocks hitting 52-week highs; rally up to 14% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex climbed 2,009 points to settle at 79,310 on Thursday. Riding the market rally, 10 stocks from the BSE 100 index hit fresh 52-week highs, touching their highest price levels in the past 12 months. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the last year and may indicate heightened market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Muthoot Microfin Q2 profit jumps 3.6 times to Rs 111 crore
items.description: Muthoot Microfin reported a 3.6-fold year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 111 crore, supported by secured lending growth and improved asset quality. Total income increased 27% to Rs 733 crore, while gross NPAs declined to 3.38%.

items.title: FIIs pour Rs 15,000 crore into Indian stocks in biggest single day buying over a year
items.description: Foreign institutional investors invested Rs 14,975 crore in Indian equities on Thursday, marking their biggest single-day purchase in over a year. The buying spree boosted market sentiment, sending the Nifty up 2.4% amid easing crude prices and improving global cues.

items.title: Sebi revises currency derivative norms for domestic investors, FPIs; allows to trade up to USD 5 mn
items.description: Sebi has revised its regulations to permit domestic and foreign portfolio investors to take positions in currency derivatives. Investors can now hold up to USD 5 million without establishing underlying exposure. The new guidelines also require FPIs to ensure their short positions do not exceed this limit. For amounts above the threshold, FPIs must have underlying exposure in Indian debt or equity securities.

items.title: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than ever
items.description: Zerodha CEO Nithin Kamath welcomed Sebi's simplified NRI account-opening rules, enabling eligible overseas investors to complete digital KYC within two to three days. Effective December 3, 2026, the framework aims to boost overseas participation in Indian equities.

items.title: Trump's Loss, Wall Street's Gain? What Could Change for AI, Defence, Crypto and Elon Musk
items.description: The blue tsunami across America has sent ripples through Wall Street, too. US President Donald Trump's massive midterm setback hasn't rattled investors. In fact, markets have rallied. The Dow jumped more than 1,500 points, while the S&P 500 posted its best session in three months. Oil prices plunged and Treasury bonds rallied.Trump has traditionally been seen as the more market-friendly leader. He has promised tax cuts, deregulation and a business-first approach. So why are investors celebrating a result that could put the brakes on his economic agenda?

items.title: Market wrap: Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance, Apollo Hospital, ONGC top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian equity markets staged a strong rally on Thursday, with the Sensex surging over 2,000 points and the Nifty jumping 576 points amid optimism following the US midterm election results. Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance and M&M led the gainers, while Apollo Hospitals and ONGC featured among the top laggards.

items.title: Sebi approves net settlement of cash market trades for mutual funds
items.description: India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has greenlit the introduction of net settlement for mutual fund schemes, set to take effect on April 1, 2027. This initiative is designed to streamline funding requirements and boost market efficiency. Previously, net settlement was exclusive to foreign portfolio investors. Eligible transactions will now be confined to sales or purchases of a specific security, while cross-scheme netting will remain prohibited.

items.title: Stock Radar: This Sensex largecap stock showing signs of reversal on daily charts; time to buy?

Experts suggest that traders can buy the stock targeting above 12,000 to 13,000 in the upcoming months. Technical indicators such as the Supertrend and MACD signal bullish momentum for the stock. The stock tested its multi-month consolidation zone, indicating a critical demand area.

items.title: Bulls roar! Market value of BSE-listed companies crosses Rs 500 lakh cr for first time as Sensex soars 2,000 pts. More upside ahead?
items.description: Indian markets rallied sharply, pushing BSE's total market capitalisation past Rs 500 lakh crore for the first time. Easing crude oil prices, renewed FII buying, a stronger rupee and improving geopolitical sentiment supported gains. However, analysts caution that sustained momentum depends on foreign inflows, earnings growth and crude prices.

items.title: 11 smallcap stocks maintain over 10% profit margin in Q1 and Q2, shares rally 150-350% in FY27
items.description: A consistently healthy net profit margin indicates a company's ability to manage costs and generate profits relative to its revenue. We screened the smallcap universe to identify companies that reported a net profit margin of over 10% in both Q1 and Q2FY27, excluding banking and financial services stocks. The screen threw up around 215 companies that met this criterion. Of these, 65 stocks have gained between 50% and 350% in FY27 so far. We have highlighted 11 stocks that have delivered price gains of over 150% in FY27 so far while maintaining a net profit margin of more than 10% in both quarters. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.description: BSE and NSE will remain closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada, while a special one-hour Muhurat Trading session will be held on November 8. Investors can also check the remaining 2026 market holidays, including Guru Nanak Jayanti and Christmas, along with key timings for the festive trading session.

items.description: LG Electronics India shares surged to a 52-week high after strong Q2FY27 results, with Jefferies retaining its Buy rating and Rs 1,950 target price. The brokerage expects 21% EPS CAGR through FY29, driven by premiumisation, capacity expansion and new business opportunities.
